arc.energy_shape_notes: One long plateau, then the turn: bright C# major verse for 4:30, an 8s dropout, a short peak burst, a 90s valley where the key turns to G# minor, a rebuild, and a finale climb that is the loudest passage in the track (-9.9dB RMS at 555s) and ends at full volume (-10.2dB) with no fade. No post-climax valley, no comedown. The voice asks the question for 7 minutes (ends 497.3s) and the last 87s answer it instrumentally, louder than the voice ever was.

generator_hints.bass: root-driven low end, darkens as the track gets louder (centroid falls to ~2520Hz in the finale)

harmony.home_scale: C# major (C# D# F F# G# A# C) for 0-270s, I-IV-V; then G# natural minor (G# A# B C# D# E F#) with E-major VI alternation to the end; tonic C# demoted to IV of the new minor home and never returns
signature_devices: Major-to-minor turn at the valley: confident C# major (key conf. 0.73-0.95) flips to G# minor at exactly 270s, the moment the RMS valley begins. The key change IS the breakdown.
i-VI vamp in the second half: G# min <-> E maj alternation, detector flipping at low confidence (0.59-0.71) because the triads share two tones (E-G#-B vs G#-B-D#). Tension via ambiguity, not cadence.
No V-i cadence anywhere in the second half; ends in i-VI ambiguity, not on a tonic arrival.
Four-on-the-floor grid at 143.6 BPM, verified by downbeat spacing ~1.65s; first downbeat at 21.55s, opening ~21s beatless.
One 8s dropout at 220-230s (-19.7dB at 225s), bracketed by segment boundaries 221.6/229.6s, placed at the end of the vocal verse as a full stop before the peak burst.
Per-minute 112.3 BPM misread at 300-360s is a tracker artifact in the sparse valley, not a tempo change; downbeat spacing holds.

tempo.feel: four-on-the-floor at 143.6 BPM, rock-stable; long steady verse plateau (~-15dB RMS for 2 minutes), then a clean monotonic finale ramp from 468s to the track maximum. No swing or tempo-change claims supported by the data.

timbre.palette_notes: Mid-bright: mean centroid 2802Hz, rolloff 5818Hz, ZCR 0.111. Darkest at the start (centroid 1151Hz, rolloff 2192Hz at 5s), brightest in the verse (3721Hz at 130s) and in the valley (per-minute means ~3250Hz at 300-360s) - the quietest section is among the brightest, i.e. exposed not muffled. Finale darkens to ~2520Hz while getting louder: low-end weight takes over once the voice leaves.
